sanskrit: gatapratyāgatākṣepaiś citraiḥ śastravighātibhiḥ vividhair vismayaṃ jagmus tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ
english: At the wondrous, weapon-shattering passes—advances, recoils, and feints of every kind—shown by those two lions among men, the onlookers were filled with amazement.

sanskrit: hastalāghavam astreṣu darśayantau mahābalau anyonyaṃ samavidhyetāṃ śarais tau droṇasātyakī
english: Displaying the deftness of their hands in the wielding of weapons, those two mighty warriors, Droṇa and Sātyaki, pierced each other with their shafts.

sanskrit: tato droṇasya dāśārhaḥ śarāṃś ciccheda saṃyuge patribhiḥ sudṛḍhair āśu dhanuś caiva mahādyute
english: Then, O lord of great splendour, the Dāśārha swiftly cut apart Droṇa's arrows in the fray with his own well-feathered shafts, and severed his bow as well.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa bhāradvājo 'paraṃ dhanuḥ sajyaṃ cakāra tac cāśu cicchedāsya sa sātyakiḥ
english: In the mere blink of an eye Bhāradvāja strung another bow, but that too Sātyaki swiftly cut to pieces.

sanskrit: tatas tvaran punar droṇo dhanurhasto vyatiṣṭhata sajyaṃ sajyaṃ punaś cāsya ciccheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then in haste Droṇa stood once more with bow in hand; yet each time he strung it, Sātyaki cut it asunder again with his keen shafts.

sanskrit: tato 'sya saṃyuge droṇo dṛṣṭvā karmātimānuṣam yuyudhānasya rājendra manasedam acintayat
english: Then, O king of kings, beholding in the combat the more-than-human feat of Yuyudhāna, Droṇa pondered thus in his heart:

sanskrit: etad astrabalaṃ rāme kārtavīrye dhanaṃjaye bhīṣme ca puruṣavyāghre yad idaṃ sātvatāṃ vare
english: "Such mastery of weapons as is found in this best of the Sātvatas was found only in Rāma, in Kārtavīrya, in Dhanaṃjaya, and in Bhīṣma, that tiger among men."

sanskrit: taṃ cāsya manasā droṇaḥ pūjayām āsa vikramam lāghavaṃ vāsavasyeva saṃprekṣya dvijasattamaḥ
english: And Droṇa, that best of the twice-born, honoured his valour in his heart, beholding a deftness like Vāsava's own.

sanskrit: tutoṣāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhas tathā devāḥ savāsavāḥ na tām ālakṣayām āsur laghutāṃ śīghrakāriṇaḥ
english: That foremost of those skilled in arms was well pleased, and so too were the gods together with Vāsava; yet for all their swiftness they could not discern the lightness of his hand.

sanskrit: devāś ca yuyudhānasya gandharvāś ca viśāṃ pate siddhacāraṇasaṃghāś ca vidur droṇasya karma tat
english: The gods, O lord of peoples, and the Gandharvas, and the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas, marked well that feat of Yuyudhāna and of Droṇa alike.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad dhanur ādāya droṇaḥ kṣatriyamardanaḥ astrair astravidāṃ śreṣṭho yodhayām āsa bhārata
english: Then, taking up another bow, Droṇa, the crusher of warriors, that foremost of those who know weapons, did battle with his missiles, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasyāstrāṇy astramāyābhiḥ pratihanya sa sātyakiḥ jaghāna niśitair bāṇais tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Sātyaki, beating back his missiles by the magic of his own weaponry, struck him with keen arrows—and that was a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: tasyātimānuṣaṃ karma dṛṣṭvānyair asamaṃ raṇe yuktaṃ yogena yogajñās tāvakāḥ samapūjayan
english: Beholding that more-than-human feat of his, unmatched by any other in the battle and joined with practised skill, your own men, who knew such skill, gave him their praise.

sanskrit: yad astram asyati droṇas tad evāsyati sātyakiḥ tam ācāryo 'py asaṃbhrānto 'yodhayac chatrutāpanaḥ
english: Whatever missile Droṇa hurled, that very missile Sātyaki hurled in turn; yet the preceptor, scorcher of foes, fought on undismayed.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja dhanurvedasya pāragaḥ vadhāya yuyudhānasya divyam astram udairayat
english: Then, O great king, wrathful, that master who had reached the far shore of the science of archery raised a celestial weapon to slay Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: tad āgneyaṃ mahāghoraṃ ripughnam upalakṣya saḥ astraṃ divyaṃ maheṣvāso vāruṇaṃ samudairayat
english: Marking that terrible foe-destroying weapon of Agni, that mighty archer raised in answer the celestial weapon of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīd dṛṣṭvā divyāstradhāriṇau na vicerus tadākāśe bhūtāny ākāśagāny api
english: A great cry of dismay went up at the sight of the two wielders of celestial arms, and the very creatures that move through the sky ceased to range the heavens.

sanskrit: astre te vāruṇāgneye tābhyāṃ bāṇasamāhite na tāvad abhiṣajyete vyāvartad atha bhāskaraḥ
english: Those two weapons, of Varuṇa and of Agni, loosed by the pair upon their arrows, did not yet clash together—and meanwhile the sun began to decline.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca paryarakṣanta sātyakim
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, and Nakula and Sahadeva, closed round Sātyaki to guard him.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhaiḥ sārdhaṃ virāṭaś ca sakekayaḥ matsyāḥ śālveyasenāś ca droṇam ājagmur añjasā
english: And led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa together with the Kekayas, the Matsyas, and the host of the Śālveyas, came straight upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ puraskṛtya rājaputrāḥ sahasraśaḥ droṇam abhyupapadyanta sapatnaiḥ parivāritam
english: Setting Duḥśāsana at their head, the king's sons by the thousand hastened to the aid of Droṇa, who was hemmed in by his foes.

sanskrit: tato yuddham abhūd rājaṃs tava teṣāṃ ca dhanvinām rajasā saṃvṛte loke śarajālasamāvṛte
english: Then, O king, a battle was joined between your bowmen and theirs, while the world was shrouded in dust and overspread with a netting of arrows.

sanskrit: sarvam āvignam abhavan na prājñāyata kiṃ cana sainyena rajasā dhvaste nirmaryādam avartata
english: All became confusion; nothing could be made out at all; and with the host smothered in dust the fighting raged on past all bounds.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca parivartamāne tv āditye tatra sūryasya raśmibhiḥ rajasā kīryamāṇāś ca mandībhūtāś ca sainikāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As the sun wheeled on, the soldiers there, blinded by the sun's rays and bestrewn with dust, grew faint and slack.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhatāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ punar āvartatām api bhajyatāṃ jayatāṃ caiva jagāma tad ahaḥ śanaiḥ
english: For those who stood firm, who fought on, who turned back again, who broke and fled, and who conquered, that day passed slowly away.

sanskrit: tathā teṣu viṣakteṣu sainyeṣu jayagṛddhiṣu arjuno vāsudevaś ca saindhavāyaiva jagmatuḥ
english: While the armies were thus locked together, greedy for victory, Arjuna and Vāsudeva pressed on straight toward the Saindhava.

sanskrit: rathamārgapramāṇaṃ tu kaunteyo niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ cakāra tatra panthānaṃ yayau yena janārdanaḥ
english: With his keen shafts the son of Kuntī cleared there a path wide enough for a chariot, along which Janārdana drove.

sanskrit: yatra yatra ratho yāti pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ tatra tatraiva dīryante senās tava viśāṃ pate
english: Wherever the chariot of the great-souled Pāṇḍava went, O lord of peoples, there your armies were torn asunder.

sanskrit: rathaśikṣāṃ tu dāśārho darśayām āsa vīryavān uttamādhamamadhyāni maṇḍalāni vidarśayan
english: And the valiant Dāśārha displayed his mastery of the chariot, tracing wheeling courses high and low and midway.

sanskrit: te tu nāmāṅkitāḥ pītāḥ kālajvalanasaṃnibhāḥ snāyunaddhāḥ suparvāṇaḥ pṛthavo dīrghagāminaḥ
english: Those shafts, marked with his name, yellow, like the fire of doom, bound with sinew, well-jointed, broad, and far-flying—

sanskrit: vaiṇavāyasmayaśarāḥ svāyatā vividhānanāḥ rudhiraṃ patagaiḥ sārdhaṃ prāṇināṃ papur āhave
english: shafts made of reed and of iron, well-drawn, of many-fashioned heads—drank, along with the birds of the air, the blood of living creatures in the fray.

sanskrit: rathasthitaḥ krośamātre yān asyaty arjunaḥ śarān rathe krośam atikrānte tasya te ghnanti śātravān
english: The arrows that Arjuna, standing upon his car, loosed when foes were a krośa off—by the time his chariot had crossed that krośa, were striking down those very enemies.

sanskrit: tārkṣyamārutaraṃhobhir vājibhiḥ sādhuvāhibhiḥ tathāgacchad dhṛṣīkeśaḥ kṛtsnaṃ vismāpayañ jagat
english: With horses swift as Tārkṣya and the wind, well-trained to draw, Hṛṣīkeśa drove onward, filling the whole world with wonder.

sanskrit: na tathā gacchati rathas tapanasya viśāṃ pate nendrasya na ca rudrasya nāpi vaiśravaṇasya ca
english: Not so swiftly, O lord of peoples, moves the chariot of the Sun, nor of Indra, nor of Rudra, nor even of Vaiśravaṇa,

sanskrit: nānyasya samare rājan gatapūrvas tathā rathaḥ yathā yayāv arjunasya manobhiprāyaśīghragaḥ
english: nor, O king, has the chariot of any other ever gone in battle as went the car of Arjuna, swift as the speeding of thought.

sanskrit: praviśya tu raṇe rājan keśavaḥ paravīrahā senāmadhye hayāṃs tūrṇaṃ codayām āsa bhārata
english: Plunging into the battle, O king, Keśava, slayer of hostile heroes, swiftly urged the steeds into the midst of the host, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatas tasya rathaughasya madhyaṃ prāpya hayottamāḥ kṛcchreṇa ratham ūhus taṃ kṣutpipāsāśramānvitāḥ
english: Then, having reached the midst of that flood of chariots, those noble horses, beset by hunger, thirst, and weariness, drew the car only with great labour.

sanskrit: kṣatāś ca bahubhiḥ śastrair yuddhaśauṇḍair anekaśaḥ maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi vicerus te muhur muhuḥ
english: Wounded by many weapons of the war-drunk foe, again and again they wheeled through their wondrous circling courses.

sanskrit: hatānāṃ vājināgānāṃ rathānāṃ ca naraiḥ saha upariṣṭād atikrāntāḥ śailābhānāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: By the thousand they passed over the slain—horses and elephants and chariots together with their men—heaped up like hills.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīrāv āvantyau bhrātarau nṛpa sahasenau samārchetāṃ pāṇḍavaṃ klāntavāhanam
english: At this juncture, O king, the two heroic brothers of Avanti, with their armies, fell upon the Pāṇḍava, whose horses were now wearied.

sanskrit: tāv arjunaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā saptatyā ca janārdanam śarāṇāṃ ca śatenāśvān avidhyetāṃ mudānvitau
english: Filled with eager joy, the two pierced Arjuna with sixty-four arrows, Janārdana with seventy, and the horses with a hundred.

sanskrit: tāv arjuno mahārāja navabhir nataparvabhiḥ ājaghāna raṇe kruddho marmajño marmabhedibhiḥ
english: Those two, O great king, Arjuna in his wrath struck in the battle with nine smooth-jointed shafts, vital-piercing arrows loosed by one who knew the vital spots.

sanskrit: tatas tau tu śaraugheṇa bībhatsuṃ sahakeśavam ācchādayetāṃ saṃrabdhau siṃhanādaṃ ca nedatuḥ
english: Then the two, enraged, covered Bībhatsu together with Keśava beneath a flood of arrows, and roared aloud their lion's roar.

sanskrit: tayos tu dhanuṣī citre bhallābhyāṃ śvetavāhanaḥ ciccheda samare tūrṇaṃ dhvajau ca kanakojjvalau
english: But he of the white steeds swiftly, with two broad-headed shafts, cut apart their gleaming bows in the fight, and their standards bright with gold.

sanskrit: athānye dhanuṣī rājan pragṛhya samare tadā pāṇḍavaṃ bhṛśasaṃkruddhāv ardayām āsatuḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, O king, taking up other bows in the combat, the two, fiercely enraged, tormented the Pāṇḍava with their arrows.

sanskrit: tayos tu bhṛśasaṃkruddhaḥ śarābhyāṃ pāṇḍunandanaḥ ciccheda dhanuṣī tūrṇaṃ bhūya eva dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: But the son of Pāṇḍu, exceedingly wrathful, with two arrows swiftly cut their bows apart once again—Dhanaṃjaya did.

sanskrit: tathānyair viśikhais tūrṇaṃ hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ jaghānāśvān sapadātāṃs tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then with other golden-shafted, stone-whetted arrows he swiftly slew their horses and the footmen with them, and the flanking charioteers of both.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhasya ca śiraḥ kāyāt kṣurapreṇa nyakṛntata sa papāta hataḥ pṛthvyāṃ vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ
english: And with a razor-edged shaft he severed the elder's head from his body; slain, he fell to the earth like a tree shattered by the wind.

sanskrit: vindaṃ tu nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā anuvindaḥ pratāpavān hatāśvaṃ ratham utsṛjya gadāṃ gṛhya mahābalaḥ
english: Seeing Vinda slain, the mighty and valorous Anuvinda left his horseless chariot and took up his mace.

sanskrit: abhyadravata saṃgrāme bhrātur vadham anusmaran gadayā gadināṃ śreṣṭho nṛtyann iva mahārathaḥ
english: Remembering his brother's slaughter, that foremost of mace-wielders, that great chariot-warrior, rushed forward in the battle, mace in hand, as though dancing.

sanskrit: anuvindas tu gadayā lalāṭe madhusūdanam spṛṣṭvā nākampayat kruddho mainākam iva parvatam
english: Anuvinda in his wrath struck the slayer of Madhu upon the brow with his mace, yet shook him no more than one might shake Mount Maināka.

sanskrit: tasyārjunaḥ śaraiḥ ṣaḍbhir grīvāṃ pādau bhujau śiraḥ nicakarta sa saṃchinnaḥ papātādricayo yathā
english: With six arrows Arjuna shore off his neck, his feet, his arms, and his head; thus dismembered, he fell like a heap of mountain crags.

sanskrit: tatas tau nihatau dṛṣṭvā tayo rājan padānugāḥ abhyadravanta saṃkruddhāḥ kirantaḥ śataśaḥ śarān
english: Then, O king, seeing those two slain, their followers rushed forward in fury, showering arrows by the hundred.

sanskrit: tān arjunaḥ śarais tūrṇaṃ nihatya bharatarṣabha vyarocata yathā vahnir dāvaṃ dagdhvā himātyaye
english: Swiftly slaying them with his shafts, O bull of the Bharatas, Arjuna shone forth like a fire that has burnt up a forest at winter's end.

sanskrit: tayoḥ senām atikramya kṛcchrān niryād dhanaṃjayaḥ vibabhau jaladān bhittvā divākara ivoditaḥ
english: Passing through the army of those two and emerging from it with hard labour, Dhanaṃjaya shone like the risen sun breaking through the clouds.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kuravas trastāḥ prahṛṣṭāś cābhavan punaḥ abhyavarṣaṃs tadā pārthaṃ samantād bharatarṣabha
english: Beholding him, the Kurus were stricken with fear, then took heart again, O bull of the Bharatas, and rained their shafts on Pārtha from every side.

sanskrit: śrāntaṃ cainaṃ samālakṣya jñātvā dūre ca saindhavam siṃhanādena mahatā sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Marking that he was wearied, and knowing the Saindhava still far off, they hemmed him in on all sides with a mighty lion's roar.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā susaṃrabdhān utsmayan puruṣarṣabhaḥ śanakair iva dāśārham arjuno vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing them in their high fury, that bull among men, Arjuna, smiling, spoke softly these words to the Dāśārha:

sanskrit: śarārditāś ca glānāś ca hayā dūre ca saindhavaḥ kim ihānantaraṃ kāryaṃ jyāyiṣṭhaṃ tava rocate
english: "The horses are wounded by arrows and spent, and the Saindhava is still far off. What course seems best to you to be taken next?

sanskrit: brūhi kṛṣṇa yathātattvaṃ tvaṃ hi prājñatamaḥ sadā bhavannetrā raṇe śatrūn vijeṣyantīha pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Tell me truly, Kṛṣṇa, for you are ever the wisest of all; with you as their guide the Pāṇḍavas shall surely conquer their foes in battle here.

sanskrit: mama tv anantaraṃ kṛtyaṃ yad vai tat saṃnibodha me hayān vimucya hi sukhaṃ viśalyān kuru mādhava
english: As for what I must do next, hear it from me: unyoke the horses and ease them, and draw the arrows from their flesh, O Mādhava."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena keśavaḥ pratyuvāca tam mamāpy etan mataṃ pārtha yad idaṃ te prabhāṣitam
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, Keśava answered him: "This too is my own mind, O Pārtha, even as you have spoken."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca aham āvārayiṣyāmi sarvasainyāni keśava tvam apy atra yathānyāyaṃ kuru kāryam anantaram
english: Arjuna said: "I will hold off all the armies, Keśava; and you, meanwhile, do here in due order what next must be done."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca so 'vatīrya rathopasthād asaṃbhrānto dhanaṃjayaḥ gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanur ādāya tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, descending undismayed from the floor of his chariot, Dhanaṃjaya took up the Gāṇḍīva bow and stood unshaken as a mountain.

sanskrit: tam abhyadhāvan krośantaḥ kṣatriyā jayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ idaṃ chidram iti jñātvā dharaṇīsthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: The warriors, longing for victory, rushed shouting upon him, judging this their opening, since Dhanaṃjaya now stood upon the ground.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ rathavaṃśena mahatā paryavārayan vikarṣantaś ca cāpāni visṛjantaś ca sāyakān
english: With a great array of chariots they encircled him alone, drawing their bows and loosing their arrows.

sanskrit: astrāṇi ca vicitrāṇi kruddhās tatra vyadarśayan chādayantaḥ śaraiḥ pārthaṃ meghā iva divākaram
english: In their wrath they displayed there their many wondrous weapons, veiling Pārtha with arrows as the clouds veil the sun.

sanskrit: abhyadravanta vegena kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabham rathasiṃhaṃ rathodārāḥ siṃhaṃ mattā iva dvipāḥ
english: With great force the warriors, lordly upon their cars, rushed upon that bull among warriors, that lion among chariot-fighters, as rutting elephants rush upon a lion.

sanskrit: tatra pārthasya bhujayor mahad balam adṛśyata yat kruddho bahulāḥ senāḥ sarvataḥ samavārayat
english: Then was seen the mighty strength of Pārtha's two arms, in that, enraged, he held off the numerous armies from every side.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya dviṣatāṃ sarvato vibhuḥ iṣubhir bahubhis tūrṇaṃ sarvān eva samāvṛṇot
english: Warding off the weapons of his foes with his own weapons on every hand, the mighty one swiftly enveloped them all with his many shafts.

sanskrit: tatrāntarikṣe bāṇānāṃ pragāḍhānāṃ viśāṃ pate saṃgharṣeṇa mahārciṣmān pāvakaḥ samajāyata
english: There in the middle air, O lord of peoples, from the friction of the densely massed arrows there arose a great blazing fire.

sanskrit: tatra tatra maheṣvāsaiḥ śvasadbhiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ hayair nāgaiś ca saṃbhinnair nadadbhiś cārikarśanaiḥ
english: There on every side, with mighty bowmen panting and bathed in blood, with horses and elephants gashed and screaming and harrowing their foes—

sanskrit: saṃrabdhaiś cāribhir vīraiḥ prārthayadbhir jayaṃ mṛdhe ekasthair bahubhiḥ kruddhair ūṣmeva samajāyata
english: and with furious heroic foes, craving victory in the fray, gathered many in one place and enraged—there arose as it were a scorching heat.

sanskrit: śarormiṇaṃ dhvajāvartaṃ nāganakraṃ duratyayam padātimatsyakalilaṃ śaṅkhadundubhinisvanam
english: Its waves were arrows, its whirlpools banners, its crocodiles elephants—hard to cross; thick with footmen for its fish, resounding with the blare of conches and kettledrums—

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyam apāraṃ ca rajo ''bhīlam atīva ca uṣṇīṣakamaṭhacchannaṃ patākāphenamālinam
english: numberless and shoreless, its dust a fearful murk; covered over with turbans for its tortoises, garlanded with foam of fluttering pennons—

sanskrit: rathasāgaram akṣobhyaṃ mātaṅgāṅgaśilācitam velābhūtas tadā pārthaḥ patribhiḥ samavārayat
english: that unfathomable ocean of chariots, strewn with the bodies of elephants for its rocks—Pārtha, become its very shore, held back with his feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tato janārdanaḥ saṃkhye priyaṃ puruṣasattamam asaṃbhrānto mahābāhur arjunaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then in the battle the mighty-armed Janārdana, unperturbed, spoke these words to Arjuna, his beloved, that best of men:

sanskrit: udapānam ihāśvānāṃ nālam asti raṇe 'rjuna parīpsante jalaṃ ceme peyaṃ na tv avagāhanam
english: "There is no well here for the horses upon the battlefield, Arjuna; they crave water to drink, yet not for bathing."

sanskrit: idam astīty asaṃbhrānto bruvann astreṇa medinīm abhihatyārjunaś cakre vājipānaṃ saraḥ śubham
english: Saying calmly, "Here it is," Arjuna smote the earth with a weapon and made a fair lake for the watering of the horses.

sanskrit: śaravaṃśaṃ śarasthūṇaṃ śarācchādanam adbhutam śaraveśmākarot pārthas tvaṣṭevādbhutakarmakṛt
english: With a lattice of arrows, with pillars of arrows, with a wondrous roof of arrows, Pārtha fashioned a chamber of arrows, like Tvaṣṭṛ the worker of marvellous deeds.
